title: Gallup indicator: Artificial intelligence (AI use at work, quarterly)
measure: % of employed US adults using AI in their role: a few times a year or more / a few times a week or more / daily
finding: Any use rose from 21% (2023) to 53% (Q3 2026) and daily use from 4% to 16%; the latest quarter added 1 point to each.
limits: self-report; 'AI' undefined; annual before Q2 2025; site still shows Q2 2026

title: Gallup: employees saying their organisation has integrated AI
measure: % of employees saying their organisation has integrated AI (yes/no/don't know)
finding: Organisational integration reported by employees rose from 41% (Q1 2026) to 49% (Q3 2026); a 'don't know' option was added in Q3 2025, so earlier readings are not comparable.
limits: question change Q3 2025; one in five don't know

title: Gallup: daily AI use by industry (May 2026)
measure: % of employees using AI daily, by industry
latest_value: Technology 42%, finance 27%, professional services 22%, other seven industries 9-15% (May 2026)
finding: Daily use is concentrated: 42% in technology against 9-15% in seven of ten industries.
limits: single reading shown by industry

title: Generative AI, adoption rate for work: employed adults (RPSGENAIUSAGESHAREWORK)
measure: % of employed adults 18-64 who use generative AI for their job
finding: Work use rose from 33.3% (Q3 2024) to 45.2% (Q2 2026), with a dip to 31.0% in Q4 2024.
limits: online panel; self-report; 'use' includes light use

title: Generative AI, adoption rate overall: working-age adults (RPSGENAIUSAGESHAREALL)
measure: % of adults 18-64 who use generative AI for any purpose
finding: Any use among working-age adults rose from 44.6% (Q3 2024) to 61.8% (Q2 2026), rising every quarter.
limits: first reading revised from 39.4% to 44.6%; self-report

title: Generative AI, work hours assisted: employed adults (RPSGENAIASSISTWRKHRSALL)
measure: % of all work hours (users and non-users) in which generative AI was actively used; midpoint of bracketed days x minutes
finding: Share of US work hours assisted by generative AI rose from 4.1% (Nov 2024) to 6.27% (Q2 2026), with a dip from 5.72% to 5.56% in Q4 2025.
limits: bracketed self-report; midpoint estimate; site shows only Aug 2025 (5.7%)

title: Generative AI, work hours assisted, by occupation group (e.g. RPSGENAIWORKHOURSASSILCIA, production occupations)
measure: % of work hours assisted by generative AI within each major occupation group
finding: A repeated by-occupation hours series exists; for production occupations it moved 1.9% (Q4 2024) to 4.6% (Q2 2026) but swings by 2 points quarter to quarter.
limits: small cells; very noisy; contradicts site gap item

title: The State of Generative AI Adoption in 2025
measure: adoption (work, non-work), share of work hours, time savings
finding: From Aug 2024 to Aug 2025 non-work use rose 13 points (36.0% to 48.7%) but work use only 4 points (33.3% to 37.4%); time saved equals 1.6% of all work hours.
limits: first-wave figure revised 39.4% to 44.6%

title: 64% of 16-24-year-olds used AI in 2025
measure: % of people aged 16-74 who used generative AI tools in the past 3 months (private, work, education)
finding: One in three EU adults (32.7%) and nearly two in three 16-24s used generative AI in 2025, but only 15.1% used it for work.
limits: first year only; breadth not depth

title: AI use by individuals surges across the OECD as adoption by firms continues to expand
measure: % of individuals using generative AI tools; % of firms using AI (OECD ICT Access and Usage database)
latest_value: 'more than one-third' of individuals (2025); ITIF reads 36.8%; firms over 20% vs 14.2% in 2024 (ITIF)
finding: More than a third of people across OECD countries used generative AI in 2025; firm adoption rose from 14.2% to over 20% (figures via ITIF).
limits: exact figures read only at ITIF (secondary)

title: The share of Americans who say they use ChatGPT has more than doubled since 2023
measure: % of US adults who say they ever use ChatGPT (2026 also by other chatbots)
finding: Ever-use of ChatGPT rose 18%, 23%, 34%, 44% (2023-26); 19% of over-65s versus 61% of 18-29s.
limits: 'ever use'; question changed 2026; one product

title: U.S. Workers Are More Worried Than Hopeful About Future AI Use in the Workplace
measure: % of workers saying at least some of their work is done with AI; chatbot use frequency
latest_value: 16% at least some work done with AI; 63% don't use AI much or at all (Oct 2024)
finding: In Oct 2024 only 16% of US workers said at least some of their work was done with AI and 63% said they did not use it much or at all (n=5,273).
limits: one reading; older than Gallup/RPS

title: Generative AI and news report 2025
measure: % using any generative AI tool weekly / ever; six countries (AR, DK, FR, JP, UK, US), ~2,000 each
finding: Weekly use of any generative AI nearly doubled from 18% to 34% in a year across six countries; weekly use to get information rose 11% to 24%.
limits: two readings; online YouGov panels

title: Adoption Monitor: How fast are individuals and firms adopting AI?
measure: compilation of individual and firm adoption surveys (Gallup, Bick et al., Hartley et al., Yotzov/Barrero/Bloom, Pew)
latest_value: 58% of US adults used genAI at start of 2026; ~a quarter of users daily (updated 1 Jul 2026)
finding: Compiled surveys show individual use near 58% at the start of 2026, but work-use estimates diverge: Hartley et al. show a decrease while Gallup and Bick et al. show rises.
limits: mixes sources with different wording

title: The Labor Market Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence (survey waves)
measure: % of workers using generative AI/LLMs at work
finding: The one US worker survey series reported as falling: work use down in late 2025 per the Stanford monitor; the 46% to 37% figures come from a secondary news page.
limits: primary paper not read; numbers secondary

title: How Teens Use and View AI
measure: % of US teens 13-17 using AI chatbots for schoolwork, and how much
latest_value: 54% for schoolwork; 10% all or most of schoolwork; 64% use chatbots, ~3 in 10 daily (Sep-Oct 2025)
finding: 54% of US teens have used chatbots for schoolwork and 10% do all or most of it this way (n=1,458).
limits: 2025 asks any chatbot; earlier years ChatGPT only

title: Student Generative AI Survey 2026
measure: % of UK full-time undergraduates using genAI for assessed work; % putting AI text directly into assessed work
latest_value: 94% assessed work; 95% any use; 12% paste AI text (Dec 2025 fieldwork, n=1,054)
finding: 94% of UK undergraduates use generative AI for assessed work and the share pasting AI text directly rose 3%, 8%, 12% (2024-26).
limits: provider changed (now Savanta, sponsored by Kortext); saturating

title: Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
measure: % of employer businesses using AI in any business function in the last two weeks (firm-weighted)
finding: Firm AI use sat between 17% and 20% for five months after the wording change, reaching 19.8% on 3 May 2026; 37% of firms with 250+ staff.
limits: wording break Nov 2025; firm-weighted; biweekly data tool not readable this session

title: BTOS AI Question Wording Updates
measure: documentation of AI question change ('producing goods or services' to 'any of its business functions')
finding: Wording changed on 17 Nov 2025 (new series from the 4 Dec 2025 release); Census calls it a level shift and started a new series.
limits: size of shift not quantified by Census

title: AI adoption rate trending down for large companies (Census BTOS, 250+ employees)
measure: % of firms with 250+ employees using AI (old wording), six-survey moving average
finding: Large-firm AI use on the old Census wording dipped from about 14% to 12% in summer 2025 on a smoothed series; raw biweekly data were spikier and ended with an uptick.
limits: smoothing artefact possible; superseded by wording change

title: The Microstructure of AI Diffusion: Evidence from Firms, Business Functions, and Worker Tasks (NBER w35141 / CES-WP-26-25)
measure: BTOS 2026 AI supplement: firm, function and worker-task AI use (Nov 2025-Jan 2026)
finding: 18% of US firms (32% employment-weighted) used AI in a business function; 57% of adopters in three or fewer functions; 66% augment only; 2% report AI-related job cuts.
limits: one wave; firm self-report

title: Tracking Firm Use of AI in Real Time: A Snapshot from the Business Trends and Outlook Survey (NBER w32319)
measure: % of firms using AI in producing goods/services (old wording)
finding: Firm AI use rose from 3.7% to 5.4% between Sep 2023 and Feb 2024 on the original wording.
limits: old wording; not re-read this session

title: 20% of EU enterprises use AI technologies
measure: % of enterprises with 10+ employees using at least one AI technology
finding: EU enterprise AI use rose 7.7%, 8.1%, 13.5%, 20.0% (2021-25); text mining 11.8%, generating language 8.8%.
limits: annual; excludes firms under 10 staff; next release Dec 2026

title: Artificial intelligence in UK businesses: 2023 to 2026
measure: % of UK businesses using at least one listed AI technology (BICS)
latest_value: ~35% of 10+ employee firms (Jun 2026); 30% of all businesses (Sep 2026, wave 165)
finding: UK business AI use roughly tripled from about 12% (Sep 2023) to about 35% (Jun 2026) for firms with 10+ staff, then was 'broadly stable' to Sep 2026.
limits: intermediate waves only in chart CSV (not read); size bases differ between releases

title: BICS wave 159 new questions: extent of AI use and share of employees using AI daily
measure: extent of AI use within businesses; share of employees using AI in daily work
latest_value: first results June 2026 (described as early indications; figures not read)
finding: The first official question on how many employees use AI daily was added in June 2026; if repeated it would be the first official depth measure.
limits: one wave; values not read

title: Analysis on artificial intelligence use by businesses in Canada, second quarter of 2026
measure: % of businesses using AI to produce goods or deliver services in the previous 12 months
finding: Canadian business AI use rose from 6.1% (Q2 2024) to 12.2% (Q2 2025) to 19.2% (Q2 2026) on unchanged wording.
limits: 12-month look-back; yes/no only

title: Adoption and investment in AI across the euro area: insights from harmonised firm-level data (ECB Occasional Paper 395)
measure: SAFE survey modules (Jun and Dec 2025), ~6,000 firms in 12 euro-area countries: any AI use and self-rated significance
finding: About 70% of euro-area firms report some AI use but only 7% call their adoption significant.
limits: abstract only; self-rated intensity

title: The state of AI (global executive survey)
measure: % of respondents whose organisation uses AI in at least one function
finding: Executive-network survey shows near-saturation (55% 2023 to 88% 2025) while official firm surveys show about 20%.
limits: self-selected large firms; ceiling reached; not re-read this session

cite: Federal Reserve Board 2026 (Survey of Business Uncertainty)
title: Monitoring AI Adoption in the U.S. Economy (FEDS Note)
measure: employment-weighted share of firms using AI (executive survey)
finding: Weighted by employment, an executive survey puts AI use at 78% of firms, against about 18% firm-weighted in Census data.
limits: not re-read this session

title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption by Ramp Businesses: Overall (RAMPAIALL)
measure: % of Ramp customer businesses (70,000+) with a payment to an AI product or service in the month
finding: Paid AI adoption among Ramp customers rose from 7.5% (Jan 2023) to 56.1% (Aug 2026), with monthly gains shrinking to under 1 point from June to August 2026.
limits: customer base skews to start-ups/tech; paid only; values revised vs earlier posts

title: September 2026 Ramp AI Index: Cracks in the AI thesis, part 2
measure: AI spend per employee per month (top 1% of firms); provider shares
finding: Spend per employee at the heaviest-spending 1% of firms fell 9.7% in August 2026, and Ramp says new adoption is 'decelerating'.
limits: one-month move; July revised; company data

title: Microsoft AI Diffusion Report 2026 Q1
measure: % of people aged 15-64 who used a generative AI product in the period, from Microsoft telemetry adjusted for device share, internet access and population
finding: Global use rose 15.1% to 17.8% (H1 2025 to Q1 2026) while the North-South gap widened from 9.8 to 12.1 points; US 31.3% (21st), UAE 70.1%.
limits: vendor telemetry; modelled adjustments; half-year then quarterly periods

title: Microsoft 2026 Q2 Global AI Diffusion Report (as reported)
measure: as msft-diffusion
finding: Q2 2026 global use reportedly 18.8% (+1 point) with the North-South gap at 12.6 points.
limits: secondary report; Microsoft's Q2 page not read

title: Anthropic Economic Index: geography and the AI Usage Index
measure: AI Usage Index: country's share of Claude.ai use divided by its share of working-age population
latest_value: DC 3.82 top US state; Israel, Singapore, Australia, NZ, Korea top countries (Aug 2025 data)
finding: 1% higher GDP per capita goes with 0.7% higher per-capita Claude use across countries.
limits: one provider; Claude skews to coding/professional users

title: Anthropic Economic Index report, January 2026
measure: Gini of per-capita Claude use across US states and countries, Aug vs Nov 2025
finding: US states converged fast (Gini 0.37 to 0.32 in three months) but there was 'no evidence that low-use countries are catching up'.
limits: three months of data; one provider

title: How People Use ChatGPT (NBER w34255)
measure: ChatGPT consumer messages, Nov 2022-Jul 2025: adoption, work vs non-work share, demographics
finding: ChatGPT reached about 10% of the world's adults by Jul 2025; non-work messages rose from 53% to over 70%; growth was faster in lower-income countries.
limits: OpenAI staff; consumer plans only

title: ChatGPT weekly active users
measure: ChatGPT weekly active users (company-announced)
finding: Weekly users went 400M to 800M in about eight months, then took about 4.5 months to add 100M.
limits: unaudited round numbers; one product; not re-read

title: AI Search Stats 2026: market share, referral and citation data
measure: monthly visits and unique visitors to generative AI websites; ChatGPT share of visits
finding: Generative AI web visits grew 70% in a year while ChatGPT's own visits stayed roughly flat and its share fell from 76% to 53%.
limits: panel-modelled traffic; web only; apps separate

title: Digital Progress and Trends Report 2025: Strengthening AI Foundations (factsheet)
measure: ChatGPT traffic by income group; internet use and digital skills by income group
finding: Middle-income countries produce over 40% of ChatGPT traffic, but only 27% of people in low-income countries use the internet and under 5% have basic digital skills.
limits: traffic source unnamed; no low-income use figure

title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI (NBER w32966; Management Science 2026)
measure: genAI adoption, work intensity, comparison with PC and internet adoption curves
finding: Work adoption has been as fast as the PC and overall adoption faster than PCs or the internet; 1-5% of work hours were assisted in late 2024.
limits: self-report; historical curves not like-for-like

title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI (On the Economy blog)
measure: adoption X years after first mass-market product: genAI vs PC vs internet
finding: GenAI reached 39.4% of adults 2 years after ChatGPT; PCs reached 20% after 3 years and the internet about 40% after about 5.
limits: 39.4% later revised to 44.6%; chart-read comparators

title: What Work Does Generative AI Do? (NBER w35677)
measure: task-level genAI adoption indexes linked to occupations
finding: Adoption is 'widespread but shallow': in most occupations and tasks fewer than half of workers use genAI, and exposure scores explain only part of the variation.
limits: abstract read; numeric task shares from blog

title: The unequal adoption of ChatGPT exacerbates existing inequalities among workers (PNAS)
measure: ChatGPT use among 18,000 workers in 11 exposed occupations, linked to registers
finding: Use was widespread, higher among younger and less experienced workers; women were 16 points less likely to use it for work; employer restrictions held use back.
limits: 2023-24 survey; exposed occupations only

title: Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI (NBER w33777, formerly 'Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects')
measure: earnings and recorded hours of adopters vs non-adopters (diff-in-diff, admin records)
finding: Most employers in exposed occupations had chatbot initiatives, yet earnings and hours effects were precisely zero, ruling out effects above 2% two years on.
limits: early period; Denmark; retitled Mar 2026 revision

title: The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025
measure: share of enterprise genAI pilots reaching measurable P&L impact (interviews, survey, deployments)
finding: Widely reported claim that about 95% of organisations saw no measurable return from genAI pilots.
limits: not read; methods criticised; link not found this session

title: BTOS expected AI use in next six months
measure: % of firms expecting to use AI in the next six months
finding: Firms expect only 0-3 points of growth in six months; Bonney et al. put the expected level at 22%.
limits: expectations, not outcomes

title: Economists' forecasts of share of US work hours assisted by genAI (NBER w35046)
measure: share of US work hours assisted by generative AI in 2030 and 2050
finding: Economists' median: 10.1% of work hours by 2030 and 40% by 2050, from 3.35% in 2024; RPS reads 6.27% in Q2 2026.
limits: baseline measure differs from RPS; not re-read

title: AI measurement in ICT usage surveys: A review
measure: review of official AI definitions and survey questions across countries
finding: Official firm AI measures differ in definitions and questions across countries; the review proposes next steps toward comparability.
limits: pre-genAI; page summary only

title: Hours assisted per adopter (derived: hours share / work adoption)
measure: share of an adopter's work hours assisted (approx. RPS hours share divided by work adoption rate)
finding: Dividing hours share by adoption gives a flat ratio (about 14%) from Q2 2025 to Q2 2026: hours grew because more people use AI, not because users use it more.
limits: derived ratio; denominators differ slightly; check with authors
